clue.text: In the main, worms knocked back single drink

indicators.note: knocking back a drink tips it up, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a single performance is a solo
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone at sea, or among worms, downs a lone drink in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns SOLOLAP round to give the answer. 'In the main' means in the sea, where these marine worms live.
explanation.definitionFit: Palolos are marine bristle worms of Pacific reefs, famous for their mass spawning swarms at sea.

clue.text: Request return of record at leisure

indicators.note: a return here is a turning back, so the record's letters run in reverse

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
ease is leisure, freedom from work

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a record to be sent back whenever convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns LP into PL; 'at leisure' looks like a phrase, but 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To please, as in 'please do', is a polite request or entreaty; the verb sense matches 'Request'.

clue.text: A merry 12, to tell it as it isn't

indicators.note: telling it as it isn't means getting it wrong, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A jolly companion is urged to tell a tale untruthfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is JOHN: Little John was one of Robin Hood's Merry Men. The name is also ironic, since he was a giant, which 'as it isn't' winks at.
explanation.definitionFit: Little John is the giant member of Robin Hood's band of outlaws, the Merry Men.

clue.text: Idolise Len, maybe, for application to woodwork

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone adores a man named Len, perhaps for his carpentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals the anagram of IDOLISE LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil, from flax seeds, is a traditional finish rubbed into wooden furniture and cricket bats.

clue.text: A passionate 12 briefly is and isn't

parts.note: is shortened is the contraction 's
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A fervent man is said to exist and not exist at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is JOHN: St John's Passion is Bach's setting of the Passion story from John's gospel, hence 'passionate'.
explanation.definitionFit: St John the Evangelist wrote the gospel whose Passion narrative Bach set as the St John Passion.

clue.text: Name withheld from rough comedian

indicators.note: something withheld from is kept back, so a letter is taken out of the other word

parts.note: a rough is a ruffian, such as a gangster

explanation.surface: An anonymous coarse comic is mentioned without naming him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' reads as an adjective for the comedian, but it is a noun meaning a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a writer or teller of gags, a joke-telling comic.

clue.text: Bill in Rome to make fruit tree go round

indicators.note: go round places the word go around the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man in Rome to make a fruit tree spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is short for William, whose Italian form this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo is the Italian equivalent of William, of which Bill is the familiar form.

clue.text: An arty 12 in Cobbett's London?

definitions.meaning: ... John was a Welsh painter, sister of Augustus
William Cobbett called London the Great Wen; G for great plus wen gives the name

explanation.walkthrough: 12 is JOHN. A wen is a cyst, Cobbett's insult for swollen London.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwen John was a Welsh painter of quiet interiors, an artist; the second sense abbreviates Cobbett's 'Great Wen'.

clue.text: Diligent, even if inexact

parts.note: tho' is a shortened form of though, meaning even if
a rough estimate is an inexact one

explanation.surface: Being careful counts, even if the result is imprecise.
explanation.walkthrough: THO' is an informal spelling of though.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough worker is painstaking and careful, which is what diligent means.

clue.text: Loose ends sure to cause bad manners

indicators.note: loose letters are free to be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Leaving loose ends is sure to come across as discourteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' signals the anagram of ENDS SURE; 'to cause' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impoliteness, a display of bad manners towards others.

clue.text: A musical 12 felt one's collar

indicators.note: to collar is to grab hold of, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A singer called John was arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt one's collar' is British slang for arrested, but here 'collar' grabs the letters inside 'felt one's'. Elton John is the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is a British pop singer and pianist, a musical man with the theme name.

clue.text: Nigel's fantastic club in Los Angeles

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name is taken as written, the 's adding nothing
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A man's amazing nightclub is located in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges NIGEL into INGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inglewood is a city in Los Angeles County, so it lies in the Los Angeles area.

clue.text: Pirate getting to follow a socialite down under

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island
to tail is to follow someone closely

explanation.surface: A buccaneer starts trailing an Australian society figure.
explanation.walkthrough: SILVER, the pirate, is another theme John.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a silvertail is a wealthy, socially prominent person, a socialite.

clue.text: See 21
Live with a female in animal's home in Uncle Remus story?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: in places the female letter inside the home

parts.note: a stable is a home for horses

explanation.surface: Someone moves in with a woman to live in a barn, like a folk tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Remus tells the Brer Rabbit tales, where animals talk; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast fable is a moral tale with animal characters, and the Uncle Remus stories are examples.

clue.text: Floor makes an accusation; heard leaks in the paper

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: a floor, as on a ship, is a deck, and to make an accusation is to allege, so deck alleges

explanation.surface: A ship's deck accuses someone, and news of leaks reaches the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'deck alleges' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deckle edges are the rough feathered borders of handmade paper, formed where pulp seeps under the deckle frame.

clue.text: Lack of judgment? Ethnic rights wallahs, as expected, admit it

parts.note: the CRE was the Commission for Racial Equality, a British body

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: duly means as expected or in the proper way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Campaigners concede that they have been poor judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The CRE was the British Commission for Racial Equality; 'wallahs' is slang for people in charge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Credulity is readiness to believe too easily, a failure of critical judgment.

clue.text: Copper leg gets a grip

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, a copper
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A police officer gets hold of someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is the classic British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby pin is a hair grip, the sprung metal clip used to hold hair in place.

clue.text: Another arty 12 dealing blow to university down under?

indicators.note: dealing a blow to something sends that blow into it

parts.note: Aus is short for Australia, down under
a gust is a blow of wind

explanation.surface: A second artist strikes a blow at a university in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is JOHN: Augustus John was a Welsh painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus John was a celebrated Welsh portrait painter, another artist with the theme surname.

clue.text: Where, in Paris, victory secured existence for the boundless Proust, bearing potential fruits

indicators.note: the French word holds the victory letter inside it

parts.note: ou is French for where
life is existence

indicators.note: boundless means without bounds, so the name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Marcel Proust, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A French triumph secures a living for the novelist, a writer bearing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundless' strips PROUST to ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovuliferous means bearing ovules, the structures that develop into seeds, so potential fruits.

clue.text: Adopt tactic to reduce insurgent troops bit by bit

definitions.text: Adopt tactic to reduce insurgent troops bit by bit

indicators.note: taking a bit from each word in turn means its first letter

explanation.surface: Generals plan to grind down rebels gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the first six words spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attrit is to wear down an enemy gradually by attrition.

clue.text: Mystery figure in the arbour is a manufacturer of missile launchers

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the arbour

parts.note: a bower is a shady arbour
y is an algebraic unknown, a mystery figure

explanation.surface: An unknown person in the garden turns out to be an arms maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Missile launchers here are bows, which fire arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowyer is a maker of bows, the weapons that launch arrows.

clue.text: This mineral's down the toilet

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
john is American slang for the toilet

explanation.surface: Something precious has been flushed away.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue John is a banded fluorspar mined in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue John is a purple-banded variety of fluorite, a semi-precious mineral from Derbyshire.

clue.text: Happy to have first to confess

indicators.note: first puts the possessing word before the happy one

parts.note: to own is to have
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Being content to go first, someone admits everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' wants to be the definition, but it is the second piece; 'first' is a placement signal, not a letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit a wrongdoing, to confess.

clue.text: Juliet poorly portrayed by an acting 4 12

parts.note: Juliet is J in the radio alphabet
poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.walkthrough: 4 12 is SAINT JOHN: Jill St John is an American film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill St John is an American actress, a Bond girl in Diamonds Are Forever.

clue.text: A Dominican 12 (incomplete) and a sporting 4 12, noble

indicators.note: incomplete means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Patrick John was the first prime minister of Dominica
Ian St John was a Scottish footballer with Liverpool

explanation.surface: Two famous Johns, one cut short, add up to an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 12 is SAINT JOHN.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician is an aristocrat, originally a member of Rome's noble families.

clue.text: Entertainer Michael would be more or less for this sporting 12

indicators.note: less means without, so a word is removed

parts.note: Michael Barrymore is a British TV entertainer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV host's name, more or less, belongs to a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more or less' looks like 'roughly', but means the surname minus MORE. Barry John was a Welsh rugby fly-half.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry John was a celebrated Welsh rugby union fly-half of the late 1960s and early 1970s.

clue.text: North American girl taking cocaine thus

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An American woman is snorting drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocaine is usually snorted, through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasally means through the nose, the usual way cocaine is taken.

clue.text: A 12 of the Church, religious leader during plague

indicators.note: during puts the leader inside the plague word

parts.note: to plague is to pester

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchman leads worship during an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: Prester John was a legendary Christian priest-king.
explanation.definitionFit: Prester John was a legendary priest-king of a lost Christian realm, a churchman named John.
